name: stri_match_first_regex
title: Extract Regex Pattern Matches, Together with Capture Groups

origin.description: Extract the first regular-expression match and its capture groups.
origin.usage: stri_match_first_regex(str, pattern, cg_missing = NA_character_, ..., opts_regex = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: cg_missing
arguments.text: Text used for a group that did not participate. The default is NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is cg_missing. A miss fills that pattern's own columns with cg_missing, and extra columns beyond that pattern stay NA. A missing string stays NA. Named groups label the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive. The width is one plus the largest number of groups among the patterns. An empty character vector still takes that width, and a single named pattern still sets the column names.
origin.value: A character matrix with one row per string.
origin.example:
result <- stri_match_first_regex("abcd", "^(:)?([^:]*)(:)?$")
shown <- ifelse(is.na(result), "NA", result)
cat(paste0('stri_match_first_regex("abcd", "^(:)?([^:]*)(:)?$") returns ', paste(shown, collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Extract the first regular-expression match and its capture groups.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: cg_missing
arguments.text: Text used for a group that did not participate. The default is NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the regex settings that were supplied.

translation.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is cg_missing. A miss fills that pattern's own columns with cg_missing, and extra columns beyond that pattern stay NA. A missing string stays NA. Named groups label the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive. translation.value: A list of rows, one per string.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA, is_na
from stringi.regex import stri_match_first_regex
result = stri_match_first_regex("abcd", "^(:)?([^:]*)(:)?$")[0]
shown = ", ".join("NA" if is_na(item) else item for item in result)
print('stri_match_first_regex("abcd", "^(:)?([^:]*)(:)?$") returns ' + shown + '.')
